terms: Reuse, redistribution and automated-access terms not confirmed. Public lookup access does not establish an open-data license.
update_frequency: Not confirmed; individual record dates do not establish the refresh schedule or completeness of the public portal.
title: Building permits, applications and licenses
publisher: City of New Haven; hosted by Municity / CitySquared
description: Find permit, application, license and certificate records associated with a New Haven address or parcel. Resolve the property to a Municity parcel using its parcel key or confirmed map location, then retrieve the records linked to that parcel and compare their addresses with your starting property record.
access: Address and parcel matching through public JSON queries; JavaScript portal also available
formats: JavaScript web portal (landing page located; interactive search not independently tested)
fields: Municity's internal parcel identifier, used to request the parcel's related records. It is distinct from the city GIS parcel_id and the assessor's account_number.
Parcel lookup key. In the tested example, removing slash separators from the assessor MBLU produced the matching PrintKey; a general join has not been established. Preserve leading zeros.
The parcel's published legal address. Compare it with the starting address and individual record addresses; a parcel may have a different legal address from a storefront.
Coordinates returned for the sample parcel; the matching point lookup was tested.
Permit: Permit_ID, PermitNo, PermitType, PermStatus, PermitDate
Permit identifier, number, type, source status and permit date as published.
Application: Application_ID, ApplicationNumber, PermitApplicationType, PermitApplicationStatus, ApplicationDate
Application identifier, number, type, source status and application date. An application is distinct from an issued permit.
License: License_ID, LicenseNumber, LicenseType, Status, Date, ExpirationDate
License identifier, number, type, source status and dates. Presence of a license record does not establish current validity.
Certificate identifier, number, type and date. Interpret the certificate type rather than assuming every record is a certificate of occupancy.
Published property address, free-text work description and declared construction cost where present. Fields and null values vary by record kind; descriptions can contain personal details.
steps: Start with a property address or parcel record. Use the property assessment lookup or parcel and address layers to identify its assessor MBLU and confirm its location. The New Haven Municity portal provides a separate browser route; it requires JavaScript and its interactive search has not been independently tested here.
Follow the reproducible parcel lookup recipe for read-only JSON requests. Use Accept: application/json and SourceId: 2 headers; no credential or provider key was needed for the tested requests.

Try the tested PrintKey query for 155 Temple Street: 241 0234 00200. Check that exactly one rows entry has Parcel_ID 13397 and the expected LegalAddress. For an assessor MBLU such as 241/ 0234/ 00200/ /, remove the slash separators, trim segments and preserve leading zeros before checking the match.

If the MBLU is missing or has no match, try the tested point query as an example, substituting coordinates confirmed to lie on the intended property. Compare the returned Parcel_ID, PrintKey and LegalAddress with the starting property record. Investigate multiple results or differing addresses rather than choosing the first match.

Open the tested parcel-record query using the verified Municity Parcel_ID. Inspect Permit, Application, License and Certificate arrays separately. Carry the parent Parcel_ID, PrintKey and LegalAddress alongside each record's kind, identifier, number, type, status and date to preserve the property association.

Compare each record's LegalAddress, where present, with the parcel and starting address. Investigate corner addresses, address ranges and multiple units; keep unmatched or ambiguous records separate. A parcel match alone does not identify a particular suite. When combining groups, check applications sharing a permit number before counting them as separate projects. Select only needed fields and review descriptions for personal details before sharing.
contact: City of New Haven Building Department for building-permit questions; a current public contact and responsibility for other record kinds have not been independently confirmed.
limitations: On November 16, 2026, PrintKey 241 0234 00200 returned one parcel: Parcel_ID 13397, LegalAddress 155 TEMPLE ST. A point query at latitude 41.30570527, longitude -72.92722431 returned the same parcel. This is one commercial-property example, not validation of every address or parcel join.

The parcel's Children response contained 98 Permit, 38 Application, 17 License and one Certificate records before any de-duplication. These are observed sample counts, not citywide totals or a guarantee of complete property history.

The tested JSON endpoints are a vendor service used by the public portal, not a confirmed supported or versioned open-data API. Availability, schema stability, rate limits, pagination, bulk exports and service commitments remain unconfirmed. The PrintKey example requests at most five matches.

The portal's JavaScript landing page was located; its interactive search, document downloads and inspection records were not independently tested. The JSON workflow did not validate inspection details or download documents.

Responses may include nested contacts, owner and mailing details, and personal information within descriptions. Do not redistribute whole responses; use a field allowlist and review free text. No raw vendor records are included in this directory.

Record kinds use different type, status and date fields. An application is not an issued permit, a historical license may have expired, and a certificate is not automatically an occupancy approval. A missing result does not prove that no permit or municipal record exists.

A parcel or building match does not establish an exact storefront or suite, current use, completed work, legal compliance, availability or permission to operate. Confirm consequential interpretations with the responsible city office.

Historical coverage, refresh responsibility, reuse rights and bulk-access costs remain unknown. The weekly and on-demand source checker covers only the documented parcel sample, selected fields and related-record groups; a passing run does not renew this readiness assessment or certify wider coverage.
next: Test more properties, alternate legal addresses, ambiguous parcels, empty results and MBLU mismatches before generalizing the sample lookup.
Confirm supported API access, request limits, pagination, historical coverage, bulk exports, costs and reuse terms with the city or vendor.
Verify browser search, inspection and document access, record-type definitions, date semantics and the departmental correction route.
Assign an entry maintainer and review changes or failures reported by the shared source-check workflow before updating documented claims.

evidence.note: Automates the documented PrintKey-to-parcel and point-to-parcel comparison plus four related-record groups and selected-field checks. Regression tests use synthetic records and exercise ambiguous identity, schema changes, blocked access, malformed responses, limits and summary privacy.

The shared weekly and on-demand validation workflow includes the permits selection. The generated source page links each published result to its exact run and checked code revision. Only summaries are published; readiness dates remain separately maintained.

Live read-only point query on November 16, 2026 returned HTTP 200 and the same parcel identifier, PrintKey and legal address as the PrintKey request. Only this location was checked.

build_readiness.summary: One commercial-property workflow was reproduced: PrintKey and point searches resolved the same parcel, then its related records returned four inspected record groups. This supports that example, not citywide or bulk use.
preparation: Normalize and independently verify parcel identifiers or map pins; handle missing and ambiguous matches explicitly.
Preserve record kinds and source field meanings, review duplicate applications and select only needed fields; redact personal details before sharing.
Test additional properties and confirm supported access, coverage, request limits, freshness, costs and reuse terms before broader use.
